correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly handles all-good (not EFX0) deletions: a zero-valued item in the left/right neighbor bundle forces a stronger load inequality. The two shifted length-three inequalities are necessary/sufficient for n>=3. Weighted closed walks enumerate all and only labeled endpoint orientations. Both small matrix determinants are exact finite identities, reconstructed by integer Newton identities; an independently implemented direct EFX checker examined 491320 orientations in 21 complete finite cases. Infinity relies on the proved bijection, not experiments.

value.rationale: Enumerating fair orientations and their frequency is a motivated quantitative refinement of binary all-good EFX graph allocations, distinct from existence: random orientations can be fair with exponentially small sharp probability. The strict deletion quantifier yields a nontrivial three-local constrained language and q=2/3 cubic recurrences, not a mere binomial count. The q=2 and q=3 probability bases differ substantially and are exact for every cycle size.
